name: Dropbox
description: Dropbox is a cloud content and file-collaboration platform for storing, syncing, sharing, recovering, and transferring files across devices. Team plans add centralized administration, team folders, sharing controls, longer recovery windows, and additional security features; Dropbox also includes PDF editing and limited signature-request capabilities inside its broader content workflow.
best_for: Individuals and teams that need dependable cloud file sync, shared folders and links, version recovery, large-file transfer, and business administration without moving their primary content workflow into a project-management system.
features: Cloud file storage and sync across connected devices
Shared files, folders, and links with view/edit permissions and sharing controls
File recovery and version history, with longer recovery windows on higher plans
Dropbox Transfer for sending large files without requiring recipients to have a Dropbox account
PDF editing, annotation, self-signing, and limited signature-request capability in current Dropbox plans
Team folders, groups, roles, centralized billing, and admin controls on business plans
Dropbox App Center and Business API integrations for connecting third-party productivity, security, and administration tools

pricing.starting_price: Free (Basic, 2 GB); paid pricing varies by region and billing cycle

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.notes: Free plan with 2 GB of storage for storing and sharing files.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.notes: Paid personal plan. Current published price varies by locale and billing cycle; the plan includes 2 TB storage and 30-day file recovery.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.notes: Paid team/professional plan with team storage, admin controls, file sharing, PDF editing/signing, and a free-trial option. Published price varies by locale and billing cycle.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.notes: Paid team plan for 3 or more people with larger pooled storage, one-year recovery, tiered admin controls, SSO, advanced key management, and additional security capabilities. Published price varies by locale and billing cycle.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Contact sales for customized users, storage, enterprise security, integrations, and support.

pros: Maintains a permanent free Basic tier rather than offering only a time-limited trial
Combines file sync, sharing, recovery, transfer, PDF workflows, and team administration in one content platform
Official business tooling includes an App Center and Business API for third-party security, compliance, and administration integrations
cons: Paid pricing is locale- and billing-cycle-dependent, so the public plan page does not expose one universal price that applies globally
Advanced controls such as tiered-admin management, SSO, advanced key management, and some security features are limited to higher plans
Dropbox includes PDF signing and signature-request features, but teams needing a dedicated end-to-end e-signature or contract workflow may still prefer a specialist agreement product

faq.question: Does Dropbox have a free plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Dropbox Basic is a permanent free plan with 2 GB of storage for storing and sharing files.

faq.question: Does Dropbox include electronic signatures?
faq.answer: Dropbox's current plan comparison includes PDF signing and limited signature requests inside Dropbox. Dedicated Dropbox Sign settings and integrations remain a distinct workflow, so Miloosh does not treat the core Dropbox product as a full substitute for every specialist e-signature platform.

alternatives.name: Notion
alternatives.description: A collaborative workspace combining documents, wikis, databases, and lightweight project organization.
alternatives.best_for: Teams whose priority is structured collaborative knowledge and project content rather than general-purpose file sync and cloud storage.

alternatives.name: Confluence
alternatives.description: A team knowledge and documentation platform for creating, organizing, and collaborating on internal content.
alternatives.best_for: Organizations that primarily need a structured team knowledge base instead of a general cloud file repository.
